mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met, or the trigger fires but the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in housing starts (HOUST) above their 12-month moving average signals weakening aggregate demand but a nascent housing recovery, which historically precedes a muted S&P 500 response over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > 12-month MA
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically greater than zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) drop below 4% while payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth remains flat signals labor market tightness without wage acceleration, which historically precedes a positive S&P 500 return over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate earnings growth without inflation risk.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 70% of triggered instances, or the mean return is not statistically above zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days unless offset by strong consumer demand proxies.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically below zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPIAUCSL) above 0.4% signals unexpected inflation, which raises real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered instances, or the median return is not statistically below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sequential rise in retail sales (RSAFS) above its 6-month moving average for two consecutive months signals improving consumer demand, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days in non-recessionary regimes.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 6-month MA for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically above zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5% for three consecutive months signals a deepening labor market weakness, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days unless offset by strong monetary easing.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a broad-based expansion in supply capacity, which historically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in non-inflationary regimes.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically above zero at 90% confidence.
